newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two Mexican crude ports shut amid strong winds.
newsitem.headline: Two Mexican crude ports shut amid strong winds.

text.p: Mexican crude ports Pajaritos in Veracruz state and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state were shut at 1200 local/1800 GMT Tuesday because of strong winds, port authorities told Reuters.

Winds were reported at 40 to 50 kilometers in the Veracruz state port, and at 25 to 30 kilometers at the Tabasco port. A spokeswoman at Dos Bocas said winds were expected to increase up to 85 km per hour by later in the day.

The third and largest of Mexico's crude shipping ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, was still open at 1630 local/ 2230 GMT, although stronger winds were expected for nightfall, Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) official Salvador Palomero said.

A total of eight ports were reported closed in the Communications and Transport Ministry's 1500 local/2100 GMT meteorological bulletin, as a cold front moved its way southeast at 20 knots (38 km/22 miles per hour).
Winds in the Gulf of Mexico were expected to reach at least 66 km/39 miles per hour with waves from nine to 12 feet high.
